digests.title: AI 日报｜11月23日：数学证明声明待验证，Agent 工具链持续扩展
digests.summary: 人机协作证明黎曼猜想的声明引发讨论，但材料未提供验证结论；ChatGPT/Codex 桌面端征集更新反馈，Agent 技能生态扩展，免费试用的 Token 滥用风险值得关注。[S27][S11][S23][S25]
digests.content:
## 今日重点

### 黎曼猜想证明声明引发关注，不能等同于问题已解决

Simon Willison 摘录的 Levent Alpöge 声明称，他与 Claude 合作发现了黎曼猜想的证明，方法还可延伸至广义黎曼猜想，并称已完成不依赖假设的形式化论证。**这些是当事人的主张；所给材料未包含证明全文、形式化产物或独立验证结论，不能据此宣布猜想已获证明。**[S27]

另一则摘录中，Ravi Vakil 介绍了 Alessandro Masullo 的广义黎曼猜想候选证明，称 Brian Conrad 已持续审阅数月并提供反馈，且该工作没有使用 AI。这是另一项候选证明工作，不构成对 Alpöge 声明的交叉验证。[S28]

讨论的另一焦点是人机协作方式：Aaron Levie 将其解读为跨越人类信息处理限制的潜在变化；另一组帖子则强调，与模型协作推进前沿本身仍是一项技术能力。**这些属于观点与推断，而非证明有效性或科研生产率提升的实证结果。**[S7][S4][S5][S6]

## Builder 动态

- **ChatGPT/Codex 桌面端继续迭代。**11月22日的帖子称，团队正在准备另一次较大更新，并征集上一轮更新后仍需改进的问题。材料未披露具体功能、版本号和下一次发布时间。[S11]
- **llm-gemini 0.38.1 补齐推理档位支持。**该版本修复了 Gemini 4 Hydrogen、Neon 的 `xhigh` 设置支持。作者给出的 Hydrogen 单次示例中，从 `high` 切换至 `xhigh` 后，输出由 5,311 Token 增至 31,477 Token，费用由 3.99 美分增至 23.61 美分；这说明该示例的资源消耗显著增加，不代表所有任务都有同等收益。[S26]
- **GitHub Issues 被用于协调 Agent 群体。**Amjad Masad 的帖子称，一个高中生正在尝试将 GTA6 重新编译至 PC，并用 Issues 分配 Agent 任务。材料未提供可运行成果或完成度验证；值得跟踪的是任务协调方式，而非把移植视作已经完成。[S12]

## 开源趋势

以下信息来自发布帖与仓库简介，不代表已审阅代码、许可证或验证效果。

- **技能框架与插件规范成为工具层重点。**`obra/superpowers` 定位于 Agent 技能框架与软件开发方法论；`cursor/plugins` 提供 Cursor 插件规范及官方插件；`google-labs-code/stitch-skills` 称遵循 Agent Skills 开放标准，面向 Stitch MCP 与多种编码 Agent。[S14][S17][S23]
- **专业任务被封装为可复用技能。**`Claude-BugHunter` 简介列出 82 项技能、15 个斜杠命令及 681 个已披露报告模式；`diagram-design` 面向编码助手提供 45 类图表的 HTML、SVG 设计；`app-store-compliance` 将应用商店拒审模式、隐私检查和提交前检查整理为开放手册与 Agent 技能。[S13][S21][S24]
- **Agent 的软件与数据入口继续扩展。**`CLI-Anything` 以让软件具备 Agent 原生接口为目标；Firecrawl 简介称可通过一个 API 搜索、抓取并访问 550 多个数据提供方。前者是项目目标，后者是项目自述，材料未提供覆盖与效果测试。[S15][S18]
- **Amuse 宣布开源。**Amjad Masad 称该项目由 Replit Missions 构建，但所给帖子没有披露功能、许可证或技术细节。[S9]

**趋势判断：**这批项目呈现出从通用编码助手向技能、接口和领域工作流扩展的方向；但材料没有 Star 增长、下载量或活跃用户数据，不能据此判断采用率或热度排名。[S13][S14][S15][S17][S23][S24]

## 值得阅读

### Muru：资深开发者如何为 AI 辅助工程设定标准

Simon Willison 介绍了 mod_wsgi 发起者 Graham Dumpleton 的新项目 Muru：一款 AI 辅助开发、面向 Python ASGI/WSGI 应用的 Rust 服务器。其开发记录涉及进程模型、开发环境 HTTPS、金丝雀发布、Kubernetes、扩缩容与可观测性，适合观察 AI 如何参与持续性的基础设施工程，而非只看一次性代码演示。材料没有给出性能基准或生产可靠性验证。[S29]

### Select Styling Specimens：让模型生成可比较的设计样本

作者让 Claude Fable 5.2 制作展示 HTML `select` 样式的页面，再通过试验选择 CSS 方案。这个案例的参考价值在于把模型用于生成可比较的候选样本，再由开发者选择；文中展示不等于覆盖所有桌面与移动浏览器的兼容性测试。[S30]

## 观察

### 免费试用正在暴露 Token 转售与代理滥用风险

据 Simon Willison 对 Claire Vo 视频的转述，ChatPRD 遭遇利用免费试用、促销码获取模型用量的滥用，其中部分用于转售或支撑外部商业活动；Claire 因此正在取消免费试用。材料没有提供损失金额、滥用比例或独立审计数据。[S25]

**编辑观察：**对 AI 产品而言，免费额度不仅是获客成本，也可能成为被转售的算力入口。该案例提示 Builder 在设计试用机制时，将额度限制、异常使用识别和单位经济性一并纳入评估；这是基于案例的风险推断，并非适用于所有产品的统一结论。[S25]

digests.title: AI 日报｜黎曼猜想证明声明待核验，Agent 工具链持续细化
digests.summary: 黎曼猜想相关证明声明引发人机协作讨论，但所给材料未证明其获独立确认；ChatGPT/Codex 桌面端继续迭代，Agent 技能与插件工具增多，Token 滥用暴露产品成本风险。[S28][S11][S13][S17][S26]
digests.content:
## 今日重点

### 黎曼猜想相关声明引发关注，不能等同于已确认突破
- **当事人声明**：Simon Willison 摘引 Levent Alpöge 的文字称，后者相信自己与 Claude 找到了黎曼猜想的证明，方法还可扩展至广义黎曼猜想，并称已完成不依赖额外假设的形式化论证。这是被转引的自述，不是材料所能独立确认的数学结论。[S28]
- **另一条研究线索**：Ravi Vakil 的引文介绍，Alessandro Masullo 也有广义黎曼猜想的候选证明，Brian Conrad 已持续审阅数月并提供反馈；该工作被明确描述为未使用 AI。引文仍将其称为候选证明，而非已获最终确认的成果。[S29]
- **编辑判断**：讨论应区分“提出证明”“形式化声明”与“获得独立核验”。现有材料不足以确认上述证明成立，也不足以判断两项工作的关系。社交平台已出现将其称为“突破”的评论，报道不宜直接沿用这一确定性表述。[S7][S28][S29]

### Token 滥用正在影响 AI 产品的试用策略
据 Simon Willison 对 Claire Vo 视频的介绍，ChatPRD 遭遇反复注册免费试用、套用促销码，以及借其 Agent 获取算力或开展其他商业活动的滥用；Claire 正逐步取消免费试用。对 Builder 而言，这个案例提示：试用额度不仅是获客成本，也可能成为被转售或挪用的资源。材料未提供损失规模。[S26]

## Builder 动态

- **ChatGPT/Codex 桌面端继续迭代**：11 月 22 日的帖子称，团队已在准备下一次较大更新，并就前一天的桌面应用更新征集反馈。现有信息没有列出已上线功能或下一版发布时间，不宜据此扩写更新清单。[S11]
- **Muru：AI 辅助开发 Python 应用服务器**：据介绍，mod_wsgi 发起者 Graham Dumpleton 正使用 AI 辅助构建 Rust 服务器 Muru，目标是支持 ASGI、WSGI 应用的开发与生产运行。他持续公开架构和开发过程，涉及 worker、发布、容器、扩缩容及追踪等主题；材料未提供性能对比或成熟度验证。[S30]
- **Amuse 宣布开源**：Amjad Masad 发帖称，由 Replit Missions 构建的 Amuse 已开源。所给文本没有项目功能、许可证或部署方式，暂只能确认这项开源声明。[S9]

## 开源趋势

以下依据仓库简介整理；所给材料没有 Star 增量、下载量或使用数据，因此不能据此判断热度排名。

| 方向 | 项目与具体看点 |
| --- | --- |
| 安全技能 | **Claude-BugHunter**：简介列出 82 项技能、15 个斜杠命令，以及覆盖 24 类核心漏洞的 681 个已披露报告模式，面向漏洞挖掘与外部红队工作。[S13] |
| 开发方法与扩展 | **superpowers** 自述为 Agent 技能框架与软件开发方法；**cursor/plugins** 提供 Cursor 插件规范及官方插件。[S14][S17] |
| 软件接口 Agent 化 | **CLI-Anything** 以让软件具备面向 Agent 的命令行接口为目标；这是项目定位，不能理解为已适配所有软件。[S15] |
| 跨工具技能 | **stitch-skills** 面向 Stitch MCP server，简介称遵循 Agent Skills 开放标准，适配多种编码 Agent。[S23] |
| 数据接入 | **Firecrawl** 将搜索、抓取和数据访问整合到一个 API，简介称可访问 550 多个数据提供方；实际覆盖与服务条件未在材料中展开。[S18] |
| 垂直工作流 | **diagram-design** 提供 45 类图表的 HTML、SVG 设计能力；**app-store-compliance** 将商店拒审模式、隐私检查和提交前检查整理为手册与 Agent 技能。[S21][S24] |

**趋势判断**：这批项目的共同方向，是把开发方法、工具接口和领域检查项封装成 Agent 可调用的组件，而不只是发布独立聊天产品。这是对本批样本的归纳，不代表整个开源生态的统计结论。[S13][S14][S15][S23][S24]

## 值得阅读

1. **Muru 开发记录：经验如何参与 AI 编程。** 摘录强调，即使 AI 承担大量表层工作，判断“哪里还不够好”仍依赖开发者积累。适合关注 AI 辅助工程实践、而非只看生成速度的读者。[S30]
2. **PostgreSQL 19 的 `WAIT FOR LSN`。** 11 月 19 日的文章介绍，通过等待备库回放到指定日志位置，让后续查询读到此前在主库完成的写入；还说明了可选超时的行为。这是早于本期主要动态的工程阅读补充。[S25]
3. **llm-gemini 0.38.1：推理档位与成本。** 作者称此次修复补上部分模型的 `xhigh` 设置；其示例中，同一模型从 `high` 切换至 `xhigh` 后，输出 Token 从 5,311 增至 31,477，费用从 3.99 美分增至 23.61 美分。这只是单个示例，不足以证明更高档位对所有任务都更划算。[S27]

## 观察

- **人机协作能力仍值得单独评估。** trq212 的连续帖子认为，与模型合作推动前沿本身就是技术能力，并表示尚未看到这项能力的收益递减。这是作者观点；它与 Muru 开发记录中强调人的质量判断相呼应，但不能替代生产率实测。[S4][S5][S6][S30]
- **多 Agent 协作出现可跟踪的组织线索。** Amjad Masad 转述一名高中生尝试让 GTA6 在 PC 上运行，并强调通过 GitHub Issues 协调 Agent 群。值得继续观察的是任务拆分与验收机制；材料没有代码、演示或独立验证，不能确认移植进度与效果。[S12]
- **供应商数据回传疑问尚缺证据。** swyx 发帖质疑某些提供方是否在秘密回传数据，但文本没有指明提供方、回传内容或技术证据。目前只能记录为待核实质疑，不能据此认定存在隐私违规。[S1]

items.title: This post nails why we why we should take the Riemann Hypothesis breakthrough very seriously, even beyond math
items.excerpt:
This post nails why we why we should take the Riemann Hypothesis breakthrough very seriously, even beyond math. We’re entering an era where solving problems will look very different from how we solved them in the past.

“This is not theory-building in the usual sense. It is something much weirder and more alien. The best human mathematicians know how to build theory, painstakingly, to reach a goal. But no human brain, on its own, is capable of creating a wormhole that requires a 25,000 page long tour through existing infrastructure with no obvious or realistic connection to the goal. But huge credit to Levent here: I think no current AI, on its own, is capable of this either.”

It used to be the case that to solve a particular problem - code, life sciences, math, cyber, engineering, and so on - you were ultimately bound by how much information an individual or team could retain and understand about the space. More information or more team members don’t always help, because it gets harder to connect the dots or coordinate amongst everyone. AI changes that completely. 

For the first time ever we can decouple the human context limits and ability to work through information from our ability to drive productivity or discoveries. This is likely not just a small increase in the kinds of discoveries we can drive, but a qualitative shift in human output. 

Now every single form of prior art, insight, past research, past decision, or unrelated breakthrough, can be used for the discovery or creation of something new. This is useful for anything from cybersecurity to life sciences research. Agents will be able to correlate entirely unrelated work to a separate project; scan every bit of data in your enterprise for solving a problem; and so on. 

The solutions may not be as elegant

items.title: Token fraud is here and it’s BAD (YouTube)
items.excerpt: Token fraud is here and it’s BAD (YouTube) Claire Vo runs ChatPRD , an AI platform that helps product managers "turn an idea into a spec". The product has been live since the GPT-4 era, and Claire has been building it in public for much of that time. In this YouTube video (see also the accompanying Twitter post ) Claire describes the flood of token fraud she has seen from groups abusing the product's free trial, sometimes just to get free AI usage but often to resell tokens or run other commercial enterprises on top of the ChatPRD agent. I am funding a international Roblox and Fortnite map studio. They run a loop of free trials and promo codes and then tunnel to my agent and use it to build Roblox and Fortnite maps. Apparently one of the common prompts Claire saw running through her agent involved SVGs of pelicans riding bicycles! Presumably the token scammers are using that to help sniff the underlying models - different model families have a definite signature, and I've used it like this in the past to try and guess the identity of stealth preview models on platforms like OpenRouter. Claire is winding down her free trials entirely, which sadly looks like the right decision in the face of this abuse. Tags: youtube , ai , generative-ai , llms , pelican-riding-a-bicycle , ai-misuse

items.title: llm-gemini 0.38.1
items.excerpt: Release: llm-gemini 0.38.1 Gemini 4 Carbon only supports low , medium and high reasoning levels - but Gemini 4 Hydrogen and Gemini 4 Neon both have an extra xhigh level. I missed that when I added those models to the llm-gemini plugin, which is now fixed in this dot release. The xhigh setting for Hydrogen makes a significant difference. I updated my Gemini 4 comparison grid - note how Hydrogen at high used 5,311 output tokens and cost 3.99 cents, but the same model at xhigh used 31,477 output tokens, cost 23.61 cents, and produced a pelican that's competitive with Gemini 4 Neon: Tags: gemini , llm , llm-reasoning , pelican-riding-a-bicycle , ai , llms , google , generative-ai

items.title: Quoting Levent Alpöge
items.excerpt: I believe I have, working with Claude, discovered a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis. In fact, the method easily extends much further, resolving the so-called Generalized Riemann Hypothesis, and I expect, with more time, the Extended Riemann Hypothesis too. Claude and I have also formalized the arguments without assumptions. It is natural to feel that this is an end, in my case a loss of a principal guiding light, but what I saw during the course of progress so amazed me that I believe it is one dawn across science of something far greater. [...] Claude and I have had a great time together with such breadth in recent months, but this time Claude far outpaced me near the finish line. No, Claude flew, and danced, and sparkled near that finish line. — Levent Alpöge , alpo.ge/remark.pdf Tags: anthropic , claude , generative-ai , mathematics , ai , llms , levent-alpoge

items.title: Quoting Ravi Vakil
items.excerpt: Alessandro Masullo has a proposed proof of [Generalized Riemann Hypothesis], and Brian Conrad has been looking closely at it for months and gave extensive feedback which is being incorporated, and it is so far looking good. It is all human, with no AI. The hope was to bring Alessandro to Stanford for a year to polish the writing and then announce it after running it by enough people. Now it seems best to put out the current draft. — Ravi Vakil , Hurried Announcement: Alessandro Masullo GRH Tags: mathematics

items.title: Muru
items.excerpt: Muru Graham Dumpleton started mod_wsgi 20 years ago, and has been thinking about the ideal way to serve Python web applications in production ever since. Muru is his new, AI-assisted Rust server that aims to provide the best possible tools for running ASGI and WSGI Python apps both in development and production. As he did with wrapture , he's been publishing an extraordinarily detailed account of the project as he works on it - as part of his development process. Here's everything he's published so far, all in the last three weeks: 2026-11-04 — Twenty years of mod_wsgi, and what comes next 2026-11-05 — A first look at Muru 2026-11-07 — Muru: looking inside the workers 2026-11-08 — Muru: how it fits together 2026-11-09 — Muru: import once, fork many 2026-11-10 — Muru: HTTPS in development 2026-11-11 — Muru: WSGI and ASGI together 2026-11-11 — AI as a lifestyle choice 2026-11-12 — Muru: releases, not restarts 2026-11-13 — Muru: canaries without a service mesh 2026-11-14 — Muru: a better tenant in a container 2026-11-15 — Muru: working with Kubernetes, not around it 2026-11-16 — Muru: scaling from what the workers report 2026-11-17 — Muru: scaling to zero 2026-11-18 — Muru: overlays on a schedule 2026-11-19 — Muru: noticing and responding 2026-11-20 — Muru: a toolbar on every page 2026-11-21 — Muru: tracing in the toolbar 2026-11-22 — Muru: when lazy imports help That post about AI as a lifestyle choice is particularly worth a read: The AI may be doing a lot of the work on the surface, but deciding what isn't good enough yet is still down to me, and twenty years of getting things wrong with mod_wsgi turns out to be useful for that. I am prepared to put in the hard work to keep polishing Muru until it is something I would trust, and something you would too. Tags: graham-dum
